1.1  CCEA Approves 8 Projects of MoR Worth Rs 20,804 Cr Across 9 Statesp.6
Exam Hints:
  • What: CCEA Approves 8 railway multitracking projects worth Rs 20,804 Cr
  • Five Project Details: Cost: Rs 10,021 CrDistricts Coverage: 17 districtsStates Covered: TN, AP, Karnataka, Telangana
  • Three Project Details: Cost: Rs 10,783 CrDistricts Coverage: 14 districtsStates Covered: WB, MP, Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh
Five multitracking projects Details:
  • Cost: CCEA approved five projects of the MoR with a total cost of Rs 10,021 Cr.
  • Coverage: The five projects cover 17 districts across Tamil Nadu (TN), Andhra Pradesh (AP), Karnataka and Telangana enhancing connectivity to 2,121 villages, with a total population of about 52 lakh.
  • Lines: The projects are expected to increase the existing network of Indian Railways by about 540 kilometers (kms). The projects include:Arakkonam – Renigunta 3rd and 4th Line – 77 kmsWhitefield – Bangarapet 3rd and 4th Line – 47 kmsHosur – Omalur Doubling – 147 kmsSalem – Karur – Dindigul Doubling – 159 kmsMultitracking of Secunderabad (Ghatkesar) – Kazipet – 110 kms
Three multitracking projects Details:
  • Cost: CCEA approved 3 projects with a total cost of Rs 10,783 Cr.
  • Coverage: Three projects covering 14 Districts across the states of West Bengal (WB), Jharkhand, Odisha, Madhya Pradesh (MP) and Chhattisgarh, will increase the existing network of Indian Railways by about 656 Kms.
About Ministry of Railways (MoR):
  • Union Minister: Ashwini Vaishnaw (Rajya Sabha- Odisha)

1.2  Cabinet Approves Enhancement of EPFO Wage Ceiling from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000p.7
Exam Hints:
  • What: GoI Increases Wage Ceiling for EPFO
  • Approved By: Union Cabinet
  • Ministry: MoL&E
  • New Limit: Rs 25,000
  • Effective from: 17 September 2026
  • Revised Expenditure: Rs 11,339 Cr, 5 years – Rs 56,696 Cr
  • EPS Contribution Cap: Rs 2,080/month.
Background:
  • The revised ceiling was come into effect from 17 September 2026(Sewa Divas).
EPFO Wage Ceiling Update:
  • Background: EPFO wage limit remained unchanged between 2004 and 2014. It was raised to Rs 15,000 in September 2014.
  • Additional Coverage: The increased coverage will widen the social security net to an estimated 51 lakh additional employees.
  • Additional Expenditure: The government’s annual expenditure under the revised arrangement is estimated at about Rs 11,339 crore (cr) and over five years the expenditure is estimated at around Rs 56,696 Cr.
  • New Cap: The monthly pension contribution, under the EPS, will be capped at Rs 2,080, up from Rs 1,250 at present.
EPFO Membership & Contribution Structure:
  • Member base: The latest EPFO data show around 7.98 Cr contributing members across about 7.68 lakh contributing establishments, while the EPS provides pension benefits to around 82 lakh pensioners.
About Employees’ Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO):
  • Chief Executive Officer (CEO): Ramesh Krishnamurthi
  • Headquarters: Delhi, New Delhi
  • Established: 1952

1.3  Government Constitutes 31-Member JPC under Sanjay Jaiswal to Examine FCRA Amendment Bill, 2026p.8
Exam Hints:
  • What: Joint Parliamentary Committee constituted to examine FCRA Bill, 2026
  • Constituted By: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla
  • Committee Strength: 31 Members (Lok Sabha Members: 21and Rajya Sabha Members: 10)
  • Chairperson: Sanjay Jaiswal (BJP), Lok Sabha MP
  • Report Submission Deadline: Last day of the first week of Winter Session of Parliament (November– December 2026)
  • Purpose: Examine provisions related to foreign contributions and regulation of NGOs.
Background:
  • JPC comprises 21 members from the Lok Sabha and 10 members from the Rajya Sabha.
  • This marks the 19th JPC constituted to examine contentious bills since 2014, and the 9th since 2024.
About Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC):
  • Timeline: The committee will scrutinise the Bill’s provisions and submit its report to the Lok Sabha by the last day of the first week of the Winter Session of Parliament (November–December 2026).
About Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment (FCRA) Bill 2026:
  • Background: FCRA was enacted in 1976 during the Emergency to curb foreign influence on politics and public institutions, and was later replaced by the FCRA, 2010, regulating foreign funding of non-profit organisations.FCRA Division is administered under the Internal Security Wing of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).
  • Legislation: FCRA Bill, 2026 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 25 March 2026 and was later referred to a JPC on 12 August 2026 amid opposition protests.
About Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA):
  • Union Minister: Amit Shah (Constituency – Gandhinagar, Gujarat)

1.4  Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 to Take Effect From October 1, 2026p.9
Exam Hints:
  • Act: Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 notified
  • Notified By: Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan, RGI
  • Effective From: 1 October 2026
  • Amended Act: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969 (as amended in 2023)
  • Purpose: Ensure timely registration of births and deaths
  • Timeline: Births, deaths, and stillbirths are generally required to be reported within 21 days
  • Delay (1–2 Years): DM / SDM / Executive Magistrate
  • Delay Beyond 2 Years: Judicial Magistrate First Class.
Background:
  • Act amends Section 13(3) of the Registration of Births and Deaths (RBD) Act, 1969, as amended in 2023, to make delayed registration of births and deaths more stringent and streamlined.
About Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026:
  • Timeline: Births, deaths, and stillbirths are generally required to be reported within 21 days of occurrence.
  • Provision: The amendment strengthens Section 13(3) of the RBD Act, 1969 (as amended in 2023), requiring approval from the District Magistrate (DM), Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM), or authorised Executive Magistrate for registration of births or deaths reported after 1 year but within 2 years, following verification and prescribed fee requirements.
About Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI):
  • Legal Harmonisation: The amendment updates legal references by replacing the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973 with the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 and revises the definition of Executive Magistrate per the new criminal law framework.
  • RG&CCI: Mrityunjay Kumar Narayan
  • Established: 1961 under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).

1.6  Agnikawach Safety Launches ‘Agni Kawach’, India’s 1st Indigenous AI Platform to Strengthen Industrial Safetyp.12
Exam Hints:
  • What: Launch of India’s 1st indigenous AI-powered safety platform
  • Platform Name: Agni Kawach
  • Launched by: Agnikawach Safety Solutions Pvt. Ltd.
  • Type: AI-integrated process-safety & consequence-modelling platform
  • Key Purpose: Ensures safety against 8 industrial hazards (jet fire, pool fire, flash fire, explosions, BLEVE/fireball, toxic dispersion, among others).
About Agni Kawach Platform:
  • Integration: The platform integrates AI, Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)-native computing, adaptive-mesh Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD), cloud delivery and risk modelling on a single safety platform, for faster risk analysis.
  • Ensure Industrial Safety: It provides safety against 8 major industrial hazards, including jet fire, pool fire, flash fire, explosions, Boiling Liquid Expanding Vapor Explosion (BLEVE)/fireball, toxic dispersion, cryogenic releases and structural domino effects.
  • Current Status: The prototype has already reached Technology Readiness Level (TRL-5).
  • Key Applications: The newly launched AI-enabled safety platform can be used across Green Hydrogen, Ammonia, Oil & Gas, Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG), Chemicals, Refineries, and other hazardous industries.
  • About Agnikawach Safety Solutions Pvt. Ltd.: Incorporated in June 2026, Agnikawach Safety Solutions Pvt. Ltd., headquartered in New Delhi, Delhi.

Highlight of the ‘RAKSHA’ Defence Framework:

  • Significance: Shifts to proactive defence diplomacy, aligns with foreign policy, and boosts India’s global security role.

Exam Hints:

  • Launched by: Union Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, MoRD
  • Launched Where: Krishi Bhawan (New Delhi, Delhi)
  • Key Objective: To create a GIS-based digital land records system
  • Budget Outlay: Rs 565.50 crore
  • Duration: 2026–2031
  • Type of Scheme: CSS i.e. 100% funding from the central government
  • Key Components: Bhu-Aadhaar or ULPIN (14-digit unique identifier for land parcel);Upgradation of high-footfall 75 SROs into modern RSKs;Modernisation of RCCMS;Acceleration of NAKSHA pilot project
Background:
  • The programme aims to build an integrated Geographic Information System (GIS)-based digital land records ecosystem, expected to improve citizen access to land-related services across the country.
About DILRMP 3.0:
  • Phase-wise Implementation: As per the MoRD, the programme will be implemented across all States and Union Territories (UTs) with 100% funding from the central government through a phased, performance-linked mechanism using the Public Financial Management System (PFMS).
About DILRMP:
  • Background: In 2016, Government of India (GoI) revamped the previous National Land Records Modernization Programme (NILRMP) (2008), a centrally sponsored scheme to DILRMP as CSS.
  • Aim: To modernize the management of land records, curb land/property disputes and enhance transparency in the land records maintenance system.
  • Key Progress: Under the previous phases of DILRMP, the GoI has digitised 99.90% of Records of Rights (RoRs) and 97% of cadastral maps, while 99% of Sub-Registrar Offices (SROs) computerised.

About India’s First LNG-Powered Train:
  • Technology: The train operates as a diesel-LNG dual-fuel Diesel Electric Multiple Unit (DEMU), using both diesel and Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG), which helps reduce diesel consumption by up to 40% and lower greenhouse gas emissions.
  • Capacity: Each DPC is equipped with an LNG tank of about 2,200 litres(l), holding approximately 950– 1,000 kg (Kilograms) of usable fuel, enabling a range of around 444 km per full load while maintaining power and operational reliability alongside diesel.
  • Transition: Indian Railways (IR) has significantly reduced diesel consumption from 293 crore litres in 2015–16 to 108 crore litres in 2024–25.
Other Railway Development Projects:
  • WAG-12 Locomotive: Flagged off by Union Minister Amit Shah, MHA from Sabarmati, the WAG-12 is a 12,000 horsepower (hp) twin-section electric freight locomotive capable of hauling load equivalent to nearly 600 trucks, enhancing heavy freight efficiency.

  • First electric train: Bombay VT–Kurla (1925)

  • When: August 2026

  • Key Rule: Ban on basement morgues
  • Temperature Norm: 4°C–8°C
Highlights of National Mortuary Standards 2026:
  • Framework: The standards create a centralized regulatory system, replacing non-uniform practices, and apply to public and private hospitals in States/UTs (Union Territories) adopting the ‘Clinical Establishment Act Standards for Mortuary, with implementation by respective authorities.
  • Infrastructure: The framework mandates ground-floor placement, waste-zone restriction, 4–8°C cold storage with minimum capacity and unique ID (identification), medico-legal separation, and a ~4,000 sq ft (square feet) autopsy facility.The block must include a 2,000-sq ft operating area, viscera storage, waiting halls, and administrative offices.
  • Staffing: It is linked to annual autopsies, requiring 2 doctors, 2 post-mortem technicians, and 2 assistants for up to 100 cases, with one additional doctor, technician, and assistant for every extra 100 cases.

  • Prior Price: Lowest price in preceding 30 days
  • Helpline: 1915

Background:
  • The amended Rules will come into force from 1 January 2027 and aim to create a more transparent, accountable and consumer-centric e-commerce ecosystem while promoting Ease of Doing Business.
Highlights of the Amendments:
  • Background: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020, notified under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, establish the regulatory framework to protect consumers from unfair trade practices in the e-commerce sector.
  • Price Transparency: Platforms must display the reduced and prior prices, with the prior price defined as the lowest price offered during the preceding 30 days.

1.57  MoF Notifies Implementation of the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026 Effective From Oct 1, 2026p.55
Exam Hints:
  • What: MoF notified implementation of the Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 2026
  • Effective From: October 1, 2026
  • Replaced: Bankers’ Books Evidence Act, 1891
  • Assent: By President of India Droupadi Murmu, on 13 August 2026
  • Objective: Modern framework for use of banking records as evidence
  • Digital Records: To use as evidence:
  • Must be true representations/extractions,
  • Show no unauthorized data alterations, and
  • Show no system tampering affecting data integrity.
Background:
  • Act received assent from the President of India Droupadi Murmu, on 13 August 2026 and will come into force from October 1, 2026.
New Act Details:
  • Objective: The act is aimed at providing a modern framework for the use of banking records as evidence in line with contemporary banking practices and technology.
  • Technology Neutrality: Act adopts a technology-neutral approach by recognising banking records maintained in physical, electronic, digital, virtual, cloud-based including backup and disaster recovery sites.
  • Bank Officials: Greater clarity provided on summoning bank officials when the bank is not a party to the proceedings, requiring the Court to record a “special cause” in writing for such summoning.
  • Digital Records: For electronic and digital records to be admissible as evidence, the law lays down three conditions:Must be true representations/extractions,Show no unauthorized data alterations, andShow no system tampering affecting data integrity.

  • Installed at: Blast Furnace 1

Background:
  • The project forms part of Tata Steel’s efforts to reduce fossil-fuel consumption and carbon emissions from steelmaking and supports its Net Zero emissions target by 2045.
About Coke Oven Gas Injection Project:
  • COG: A hydrogen-rich and hydrocarbon-rich by-product generated during coke production in integrated steel plants, traditionally used for power generation, heating applications, or flaring, containing more than 55% hydrogen.
  • Operation: The project purifies and injects hydrogen-rich COG into blast furnaces through tuyeres, enabling a three-fuel operating system that reduces dependence on carbon-based reducing agents while improving process stability, operational flexibility, and efficiency.
  • Benefits: COG injection reduces fossil fuel consumption and carbon emissions in blast furnace operations by improving gas utilisation, operational flexibility, and energy efficiency, while supporting sustainable steel manufacturing.

  • Implicit Subsidy: Domestic LPG is sold below its actual cost, resulting in an implicit subsidy, estimated at around Rs. 210 per 14.2 kg cylinder in September 2026, compared to Rs. 721 per cylinder in June 2026

4.3  UNEP Limiting Overshoot Report: 1.5°C warming overshoot is now ‘unavoidable’p.103
Exam Hints:
  • What: Release of a Report
  • Report Title: “Limiting Overshoot: Navigating exceedance of 1.5°C and pathways towards return”
  • Released by: UNEP
  • Key Finding: Global Temperature to overshoot 1.5°C in next few years
  • Stages of Overshoot Pathway: Exceedance, Plateau/Peak, Decline and Stabilization.
  • Irreversible Changes: Ice sheet loss, Amazon degradation, AMOC disruption.
Background:
  • The report highlighted that the world is now mostly likely to “overshoot” or temporarily breach the global warming temperature threshold 1.5°C above pre-industrial temperatures within the next few years.
Key Findings:
  • Global Temperature: The report projected that global surface temperature is expected to peak at about 1.8°C above pre-industrial levels even under an “optimistic scenario”.It projected that with current global policies, the global temperature is expected to reach 2.6°C by 2100.
  • Paris Agreement: In 2015, 196 countries (including India) and the European Union (EU) adopted the Paris Agreement during Conference of Parties (COP21) United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) held in Paris, France.Under Article 2 of the agreement, all member parties (nations) must pledge to keep the global average surface temperatures well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels, and ideally capped at 1.5°C
About United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP):
  • Executive Director (ED)- Inger Andersen
  • Headquarters: Nairobi, Kenya
  • Established: 1972

4.4  UNGA Adopts ‘Correct the Map’ Resolution, Promotes Equal Earth Projection Reflecting Africa’s True Sizep.105
Exam Hints:
  • What: Adoption of “Correct the Map” resolution for new world map
  • By Whom: UNGA
  • Support: 164 countries (USA voted against)
  • Sponsor: Togo; backed by – African Union members
  • Purpose: Replace Mercator map with Equal Earth projection reflecting Africa’s true size.
Background:
  • The resolution, sponsored by Togo and backed by African Union (AU) members, was adopted in the UNGA with 164 votes in favour, with support from France and the United Kingdom (UK), while the United States of America (USA) voted against and six countries abstained.
About UN Resolution on World Map:
  • Background: Mercator projection, created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator, exaggerates regions near the poles while shrinking equatorial regions, leading to misrepresentation of Africa’s actual size.
  • Resolution Scope: Titled “Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World’s Regions, Particularly Africa,” the resolution is non-binding and does not ban the Mercator projection.
About United Nations General Assembly (UNGA):
  • President: Annalena Charlotte Alma Baerbock serves as the current President of UNGA (80th Session: September 9, 2025 – September 8, 2026), and Khalilur Rahman will assume office for the 81st Session (September 8, 2026 – September 2027)
  • Established: 1945

India’s Efforts to Eliminate Child Marriage:

  • Child Marriage in India: The prevalence of Indian women aged 20-24 married before the age of 18, declined from 23.3% (2019-21 National Family Health Survey, NFHS-5) to 20.1% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).

Coastal Bank Highlights:
  • Banking Milestone: Coastal Bank, India’s first local area bank, has become the only scheduled bank headquartered in AP after being included in the RBI’s Second Schedule.

  • Capital Requirement: The bank must have an aggregate paid-up capital and reserves of at least Rs 5 lakh.
  • Eligible Entity: The bank must fall under any one of the following categories:A State Co-operative BankA company defined under the Companies Act, 1956An institution notified by the Central GovernmentA corporation/company incorporated under any law in force outside India.
  • About the Coastal Local Area Bank Limited: (Coastal LAB): It is India’s first Local Area Bank, licensed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) in 1999.

6.15  NCDEX Launches ‘RAINCHNNAI’ Weather Derivatives Contract for Chennai’s Northeast Monsoonp.135
Exam Hints:
  • What: Launch of RAINCHNNAI weather derivatives contract
  • Launched by: NCDEX
  • Where: Chennai, TN
  • Objective: Hedge rainfall-linked financial risks
  • Coverage: Northeast monsoon accounts for nearly 70% of Chennai’s annual rainfall
  • Coverage Period: September–December (NE Monsoon).
Background:
  • The cash-settled futures model covers September–December rainfall deviations in Chennai, addressing the retreating monsoon that contributes nearly 70% of the city’s annual rainfall.
About RAINCHNNAI Weather Derivatives Contract:
  • Objective: The contract, complements NCDEX’s earlier RAINMUMBAI, provides a transparent and standardized tool for hedging rainfall deviations affecting sectors like agriculture, logistics, and urban infrastructure dependent on monsoon patterns.
  • Model: It is based on the Cumulative Deviation Rainfall (CDR) model, measuring deviation from the Long Period Average (LPA) using over 50 years of historical rainfall data.
  • Features: It operates as a cash-settled futures contract with a tick size of 1 millimetre(mm) and a maximum order lot size of 50 lots, removing the need for physical delivery or loss assessment.

6.28  NPCI Releases Revised MDR Framework: 0.4% Charge on UPI Transactions Above Rs 2000p.143
Exam Hints:
  • What: NPCI releases revised MDR framework
  • Effective from: 15 October 2026
  • Above Rs 2000: 0.4% for P2M transactions, capped at Rs 300
  • Flat MDR: Rs 5 – Railways, telecom, insurance, fuel
  • Capital Market: 0.02%, Capping – Rs 300
  • Education institutions: Concessional fees
  • Exemption: Small Merchants: Rs 1 lakh collectionsNot Applicable to: RuPay Credit Card linked to UPI, Presanctioned bank credit linesFund Dedication: Tier 3-6 centres.
Background:
  • The finalized MDR framework and threshold structure take effect from 15th October 2026.
MDR Framework Overview:
  • Below Rs 2,000: Both Person-to-Person (P2P) and Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions below Rs 2,000 will continue to remain free for merchants and users.NPCI has stated that such transactions constitute more than 95% of the total volume of UPI merchant transactions.
  • Above Rs 2,000: A nominal MDR of 0.4% will apply only to P2M transactions above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300 per transaction for amounts of Rs 75,000 and above.
  • Impact: The framework ensures that roughly 96% of merchant transactions and all individual transfers remain unaffected.
  • Credit and Debit card: Credit card MDRs typically ranging between 1.5% and 2.5%, and debit card MDRs capped up to 0.90%.
Specified Transactions:
  • Flat MDR: For specified merchant categories, including railways, telecom services, insurance and fuel, a flat MDR of Rs 5 per transaction will apply to UPI payments above Rs 2,000.

Transaction AmountApplicable MDRMDR Paid by Merchant
Rs 2,000NilRs 0
Rs 3,0000.40%Rs 12
Rs 50,0000.40%Rs 200
Rs 75,000 and AboveFixed Rs 300 CapRs 300

11.18  WMO’s State of Global Water Resources 2025 Report: Global Glacier Mass Loss Continues for Fourth Consecutive Yearp.241
Exam Hints:
  • What: Release of State of Global Water Resources Report 2025
  • By whom: WMO
  • Objective: Assess global water cycle trends and freshwater reserves
  • Highlights: 4th consecutive year of glacier loss globally
  • Glacier Loss Statistics: 408 ± 132 Gigatonnes glacier mass loss (2025)± 0.4 mm sea-level rise1,400 Gigatonnes loss (2023–2025)6.2% glacier loss (2000–2025)36% global river basins below-normal flow
Background:
  • Global glacier mass loss in 2025 was equivalent to a sea-level rise of 1.1 ± 0.4 millimetres (mm), with six of the seven largest annual losses recorded in the last seven years, and cumulative losses of 1,400 gigatonnes between 2023 and 2025.
About State of Global Water Resources Report 2025:
  • Glaciers: Mountain glaciers have lost about 6.2% of their total ice mass between 2000 and 2025, with some regions witnessing declines of up to 40% over past decades.
  • Cumulative: Between 2023 and 2025, glaciers lost a cumulative 1,400 gigatonnes of water, equivalent to filling around 560 million Olympic-sized swimming pools or nearly one-third of annual global freshwater withdrawals.
  • Discharge: Global river discharge in 2025 reached a 35-year low, with below-normal flows across more than 36% of global river basin areas, based on 13 global hydrological models.
  • Water Cycle: The global water cycle has become increasingly erratic, with only 34–38% of river basins recording normal conditions compared to the 1991–2020 average of 46%.
About World Meteorological Organization (WMO):
  • Established: 1950

  • Cooling: Rising incomes and temperatures will increase air-conditioning demand, with India and Southeast Asia expected to account for 20% of global AC stock by 2035.
  • Global Trends: China contributed over 60% of global electricity demand growth over the past decade, while emerging economies continue to drive future demand increases.

  • Objectives: It is designed to explore cosmic enigmas like: dark energy and dark matter, while testing gravity at vast scales and searching for exoplanets.

  • Outlook: Following the recovery from the GSLV-F10 failure in August 2021, ISRO plans six more launches this financial year, including NVS-03, while advancing the Gaganyaan programme with its first uncrewed mission scheduled soon.

15.11  NASA Discovers Massive ‘McGetchin’ Crater from 2024 Moon Impactp.284
Exam Hints:
  • What: Discovery of massive new Moon crater named McGetchin
  • Discovered By: NASA’s Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO)
  • Crater Dimensions: 728 feet in diameter, 141 feet deep, 7 km wide, occur once every 132 years
  • Named After: Thomas McGetchin.
Background:
  • The crater is named in honor of the late Thomas McGetchin, former Director of the Houston, United States of America (USA)-based Lunar and Planetary Institute.
About McGetchin Crater:
  • Formation: The crater formed in May 2024 when an asteroid or comet fragment, estimated to be as large as a multi-storey building, struck the Moon’s surface without prior detection.
  • Dimensions: It measures approximately 728 feet (222 meter, m) in diameter and 141 feet (43 m) in depth, making it larger than the Roman Colosseum and three times bigger than previously recorded craters.
  • Features: The impact created a 7 kilometer ( km)-wide cold spot due to loosened regolith and ejected debris over 100 km, indicating higher-than-expected material dispersion angles.
  • Frequency: Such large-scale impact events are rare, occurring roughly once every 132 years, making this a statistically rare scientific observation.

  • Roadmap: The team is advancing an 8–16 core vector-style GPU architecture with an optimised compiler and toolchain, alongside a 65 nm (nanometers) Application-Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC) proof-of-concept to enable cost-effective indigenous graphics silicon using mature nodes.

Background:
  • The day commemorates the death anniversary of Mother Teresa (1997), and the term “charity” originates from the Latin word caritas, meaning love and compassion.
Background:
  • Proclamation: United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) designated September 5 as the International Day of Charity in December 2012 (Resolution A/RES/67/105).
  • First Observance: The day was first observed globally on September 5, 2013.
Significance of the Day:
  • Solidarity: Emphasises global unity and shared responsibility in addressing poverty, inequality, and humanitarian challenges.
About Mother Teresa:
  • Early Life: Born Agnes Gonxha Bojaxhiu on 26 August 1910 in Skopje, she joined the Sisters of Loreto in Ireland in 1928 and arrived in India in 1929.
  • Missionaries: Became an Indian citizen in 1948 and founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata in 1950.
  • Canonisation: Declared Saint Teresa of Calcutta in 2016 by Pope Francis.
  • Awards: Received Ramon Magsaysay Award (1962), Templeton Prize (1973), Nobel Peace Prize (1979), Balzan Prize (1979), and Bharat Ratna (1980).

About Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy:
  • Rare Progressive Disorder: Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD) is a rare and progressive genetic disorder in which the body lacks dystrophin, a protein essential for protecting muscle cells.The disorder is named after Dr. Duchenne de Boulogne, who first described the disease in detail during the 1860s.
  • Age of Diagnosis: In most countries, DMD is diagnosed after 4 years of age, with an average diagnostic delay of around 2.5 years.
  • Prevalence: Globally, approximately 1 in 5,000 newborn boys is affected by DMD.

About the Himalayas:

  • Himalayan Climate & Glacial Changes 2026: A 2026 survey by International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) reveals that glaciers in the Hindu Kush Himalaya region lost 12% of their coverage and 9% of their ice mass between 1990 and 2020, with the rate of melting doubling since 2000.Some glaciers have thinned by up to 27 metres(m) since 1975, while smaller glaciers (less than 0.5 square kilometer, sq km), which make up nearly three-quarters of the region, are experiencing faster ice loss.

Background:
  • Origin: On 26 September 2013, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) adopted Resolution A/RES/68/32, designating 26 September as the International Day, following its first high-level meeting on nuclear disarmament.
  • First Observation: The first observance took place on 26 September 2014.
Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zones (NWFZs):
  • Overview: Regional treaties recognized by the UNGA (Resolution 3472) to prevent nuclear weapons within defined regions, starting with Latin America & Caribbean (1967), followed by South Pacific (1985), Southeast Asia (1995), Africa (2006) and Central Asia (2006).
  • Arms Control Treaties: Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START) (1994–2009) between the United States of America (USA) and Soviet Union limited strategic weapons; the New START Treaty is extended till 4 February 2026, while Russia suspended participation in 2023 and withdrew from the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty (CTBT) on 2 November 2023.
United Nations (UN) - Static GK:
Secretary-General: António Guterres
Headquarters: New York, United States of America (USA)
Established: 1945

  • Species: Buellia maharajensis is a newly described saxicolous lichen, meaning it grows on rocks, and belongs to the family Caliciaceae.
  • Data: A broader survey of Mathikettan Shola National Park documented around 250 lichen species, including about 60 first-time records for Kerala and 15 new records for India.
  • Naming: Named after Maharaja’s College on its 150th anniversary, it highlights the importance of the Western Ghats in conserving cryptic biodiversity.
  • Significance: The discovery highlights the rich and cryptic biodiversity of the Western Ghats and the ecological importance of Mathikettan Shola National Park in conserving lesser-known species.
